->13. The Chapter on the Pleasant Abode<-

<margin>K 275 N 180 W 235</margin>
Then, <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss>, the Ever-Youthful, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, it is difficult, truly very difficult, for these <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings seeking enlightenment</gloss> and <term>Mahasattvas</term> <gloss>great beings</gloss> to endure this out of reverence for the Blessed One. How, O Blessed One, should this <term>Dharmaparyaya</term> <gloss>discourse of the teaching</gloss> be proclaimed by these Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas in the later times, in the final age?"

When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said to Manjushri, the Ever-Youthful: "A Bodhisattva Mahasattva who is established in four qualities, Manjushri, should proclaim this discourse of the teaching in the later times, in the final age. Which four? Here, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva who is established in proper conduct and a proper sphere of activity should proclaim this discourse of the teaching in the later times, in the final age. And how, Manjushri, does a Bodhisattva Mahasattva become established in proper conduct and a proper sphere of activity?

When a Bodhisattva Mahasattva is patient, self-controlled, having attained the stage of self-mastery, with a mind that is neither frightened nor terrified, and is not envious; and when, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva does not dwell upon any particular phenomenon, but observes the true nature <note>original: "svalakshana", literally "own-characteristic"</note> of all phenomena as they really are. This lack of scrutiny and lack of conceptualization regarding these phenomena is what is called, Manjushri, the proper conduct of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

<margin>K 276 W 236</margin>
And what, Manjushri, is the sphere of activity of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva? When a Bodhisattva Mahasattva does not serve kings, does not serve princes, high ministers of state, or royal officials; does not associate with them, does not worship them, and does not approach them. He does not serve, associate with, or worship followers of other traditions—such as wandering mendicants, pilgrims, <term>Ajivikas</term> <gloss>fatalist ascetics</gloss>, or <term>Nirgranthas</term> <gloss>Jain ascetics</gloss>—nor does he associate with people devoted to worldly poetry and treatises. He does not serve, associate with, or worship those who maintain the spells of the materialists <note>original: "Lokayata"</note>, nor the materialists themselves, and he does not become intimate with them. He does not associate with <term>Chandalas</term> <gloss>outcastes</gloss>, prize-fighters, pig-breeders, poultry-breeders, deer-
<margin>N 181</margin>
hunters, butchers, actors and dancers, or wrestlers. He does not approach other places of amusement and play belonging to others. He does not become intimate with them. Only when such people approach him does he preach the teaching to them at the proper time, and he preaches it without attachment.

Furthermore, he does not serve, associate with, or worship monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who belong to the <term>Shravaka-yana</term> <gloss>the vehicle of the disciples/hearers</gloss>, nor does he become intimate with them. He does not share a common sphere of activity with them, whether in a walking path or in a monastery. Only when they approach him does he preach the teaching at the proper time, and he preaches it without attachment. This, Manjushri, is the sphere of activity of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

<margin>K 277</margin>
Again, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva does not preach the teaching repeatedly to women by seizing upon any signs of affection toward them, nor is he desirous of seeing women frequently. He does not visit families [for social calls], nor does he think that young girls, maidens, or daughters-in-law should be frequently spoken to, nor does he exchange greetings with them. He does not preach the teaching to a eunuch, nor does he become intimate with such a person, nor does he exchange greetings. He does not enter a house alone for the sake of alms, unless he is practicing <term>Tathagatanusmriti</term> <gloss>mindfulness of the Buddha</gloss>. If he should preach the teaching to women, he should not preach the teaching even with an underlying passion for the teaching, <note>The text continues describing the purity of the Bodhisattva's intent when teaching.</note>

<summary>Manjushri asks how the Lotus Sutra should be taught in the future, and the Buddha explains the first of four requirements: maintaining proper conduct and a restricted sphere of activity. The Bodhisattva is advised to avoid worldly powers, certain ascetic groups, low-caste occupations, and inappropriate intimacy with women or followers of the Lesser Vehicle.</summary>
<keywords>Manjushri, Bodhisattva-conduct, later age, social restrictions, proper sphere, mindfulness of the Buddha, preaching</keywords>
